new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Board ABSENT - no commodity and no capture match. Pine nuts (pignoli, pinon) are not covered by any existing nut id: a distinct product sold in 4-8 oz bags at roughly $25-30/lb, several times the price class of walnuts, almonds or pecans, so bridging them onto another nut would publish a badly wrong price. Searched by food across all three spellings.

registrar_rulings.reason: Verified genuinely unpriced under any name: the only 'pine nut' strings in the whole live estate are inside couscous's EXCLUDE list (commodities.json lines 67739/67869 - couscous deliberately fences out 'pine nut couscous' flavor products, which confirms no id claims them), and 'pignoli'/'pinon'/'pinenut' appear nowhere in commodities.json, recipe-commodities.json, recipe-board-everyday.json, or smp-feed.json (swept per-file with -o context on the minified feed, not trusting one empty brace-glob). No nut sibling can carry it: mixed-nuts includes only 'mixed nuts'/'nut mix', walnuts only '\bwalnuts?\b', peanuts only '\bpeanuts\b' - none matches a 'Pine Nuts' product name, and bridging is ruled out on price class anyway (~$25-30/lb vs walnuts' live $0.265/oz = ~$4.24/lb; an alias would misprice by ~6x, the exact bread-crumbs failure). Same food different id nowhere; this is a new food to the estate, not a variant, so no allowlist pair is needed. Sole batch member - no sibling collision to read against. Separate vocabulary ruling: 'pine nuts' also needs a NEW ingredients.json row (no existing name resolves to it), macro source fdc:170591 'Nuts, pine nuts, dried' (the generic retail pignoli; 170592 pinyon is a regional different nut - do not use), and a densities.json row or UNMEASURABLE-QTY will refuse volumetric lines.
